turns.script: How do I undo my last commit?
turns.asr_text: How do I undo my last commit?

turns.text_generated:
Hey there! If you want to undo your last commit, no worries—it's pretty straightforward. Let me break it down. 

If you haven't pushed your changes yet, you can use the command: 
`git reset --soft HEAD~1`
That will undo the last commit but keep your changes in the staging area, so you won't lose any work. 

If you also want to unstage the changes, you can go with: 
`git reset HEAD~1`

And if you want to completely discard the changes, you can do:
`git reset --hard HEAD~1`

But be careful with that one—it’ll wipe out any changes in your working directory related to that commit.

Now, if you've already pushed the commit to a remote, you'll need to force push after the reset:
`git push origin branch-name --force`

Just keep in mind that force pushing can affect others working on the same branch.

So, pick the one that fits your situation, and you’ll be all set!

turns.asr_text: No, I meant undo it but keep the changes.

turns.text_generated:
Ah, got it! You want to undo the commit but keep all the changes intact. No problem at all! The best command for that is this:

`git reset --soft HEAD~1`

That’ll remove the last commit but leave all your files exactly as they were—everything will still be staged, just like before the commit. That way, you can tweak whatever you need or recommit it. Easy peasy!
